name: Wyoming
overview: Wyoming DEQ's Air Quality Division requires a construction permit before construction or modification of a source begins (WAQSR Chapter 6, Section 2(a)(i)). DEQ says Chapter 6 has no de minimis emission levels; instead, Section 2(k) lists specific activities that do not need approval. Oil and gas production sites that use Best Available Control Technology (BACT) may begin construction without prior authorization under W.S. 35-11-801(e), and DEQ's Oil and Gas Production Facilities Permitting Guidance defines that BACT. Major sources need PSD (Chapter 6, Section 4), nonattainment NSR (Chapter 6, Section 13; Upper Green River Basin ozone area), and a Title V operating permit (Chapter 6, Section 3). Applications are submitted through the IMPACT portal, and drafts are posted on OpenAir. EPA Region 8 is the permitting authority in Indian Country.

permitTypes.name: Chapter 6, Section 2(k) activities not requiring approval
permitTypes.description: No approval is needed for these activities: air pollutant detectors, recorders, combustion controllers or shutoffs; air conditioning or ventilation not designed to remove pollutants; smaller fuel-burning equipment within specified heat input and fuel limits; mobile internal combustion engines; laboratory equipment used only for analyses; installing air pollution control equipment; gasoline storage tanks at retail establishments; and other minor sources the Administrator finds insignificant (a waiver under 2(k)(viii)). Major emitting facilities under Section 4 must still comply with Sections 2 and 4. DEQ states there are no de minimis emission levels.
permitTypes.quote: The permitting rules contained in Chapter 6 of the WAQSR do not include de minimis emission levels below which facilities or projects are exempted from permitting.

quoteSource.name: Wyoming DEQ Air Quality Division: New Source Review

permitTypes.thresholds: Fuel burning equipment (other than a smokehouse generator) of not more than 25 million BTU per hour that burns only gaseous fuel containing not more than 20 grains total sulfur per 100 std. ft3, or not more than 10 million BTU/hr burning any other fuel (Ch. 6, Sec. 2(k)(iii)).

permitTypes.name: Construction / Modification Permit (NSR)
permitTypes.description: A construction or modification permit is required before work begins on a new or modified source. After DEQ proposes a decision, it advertises it for a 30-day public comment period, and drafts are posted on OpenAir. Fees are a minimum $1,000 initial fee per application plus a minimum of $105 per hour, invoiced after filing. Applications go through IMPACT or are mailed (two paper copies) to the NSR Permitting Program in Cheyenne.
permitTypes.quote: Any person who plans to construct any new facility or source, modify any existing facility or source, or to engage in the use of which may cause the issuance of or an increase in the issuance of air contaminants into the air of this state shall obtain a construction permit from the State of Wyoming, Department of Environmental Quality before any actual work is begun on the facility.

quoteSource.name: Wyoming DEQ Air Quality Division: New Source Review

permitTypes.name: Minor Source Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: Under Section 2(a)(iii), the applicant submits an as-built application. Section 2(e) requires the applicant to show compliance and that construction matched the permit before DEQ grants an operating permit.

permitTypes.name: Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD)
permitTypes.description: PSD applies to new major stationary sources and major modifications. Under the Chapter 6, Section 4(a) definition of major stationary source, the threshold is 100 tons per year for the listed source categories (such as petroleum refineries, chemical process plants, and fossil fuel boilers of more than 250 MMBtu/hr) and 250 tons per year for any other stationary source.
permitTypes.thresholds: 100 tpy for the source categories listed in the definition; 250 tpy for any other stationary source (WAQSR Ch. 6, Sec. 4(a), "Major stationary source").
permitTypes.quote: Such term also includes any stationary source which emits, or has the potential to emit, two hundred and fifty tons per year or more of any air pollutant for which standards are established under these Standards and Regulations or under the Federal Clean Air Act

quoteSource.name: EPA Wyoming SIP Table C (WAQSR Chapter 6 text)

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment New Source Review
permitTypes.description: Applies to new major sources and major modifications of NOx and VOC (ozone precursors) in the Upper Green River Basin ozone nonattainment area, with LAER instead of BACT. The minor NSR exemptions in Section 2(k) do not apply to NNSR. Section 13 does not apply in the Sheridan PM10 area, where a Section 2(c)(ii)(B) construction ban continues. EPA approved Section 13 effective July 5, 2016.
permitTypes.quote: Section 13(c)(i) provides that the exemptions in the minor NSR program (Section 2(k)) shall not apply with regards to applicability of the nonattainment NSR program.

permitTypes.name: Title V Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: Required for major sources as defined in Chapter 6, Section 3, and for other sources DEQ lists: NSPS and NESHAP sources (DEQ exempts nonmajor sources until EPA requires them to get permits), acid rain affected sources, and sources subject to PSD. EPA's final approval of the program took effect April 23, 1999. DEQ says an initial or renewal permit takes about 18 months, with public (30 days) and EPA (45 days) review. DEQ issues Title V permits outside Indian Country (per EPA).
permitTypes.quote: Wyoming established an Operating Permit Program under Chapter 6, Section 3 of the Wyoming Air Quality Standards and Regulations (WAQSR).

quoteSource.name: Wyoming DEQ Air Quality Division: Title V Permitting

oilAndGas.summary: Wyoming law (W.S. 35-11-801(e)) lets oil and gas production sites that meet BACT begin construction without prior authorization. Since 1997, DEQ's Oil and Gas Production Facilities Permitting Guidance has defined BACT for these sites; the May 2016 (8th) update merged the former Statewide and Concentrated Development Areas into one area (control levels are in the guidance entry). The Upper Green River Basin (UGRB) was designated an ozone nonattainment area in 2012 under the 2008 standard; EPA found it attained in 2016, and DEQ began redesignation in December 2024. In 2024 DEQ adopted an emergency rule to incorporate EPA's NSPS OOOOb methane rule.

programs.name: Oil and Gas Production Facilities Permitting Guidance (BACT)
programs.description: Defines presumptive BACT and permitting procedures for oil and gas production facilities, including tanks, dehydration units, truck loading and pumping unit engines. Applications are submitted through IMPACT. The figures here come from DEQ's May 12, 2016 release of the 8th update; check DEQ's NSR guidance documents for any later revision.
programs.thresholds: Controls for single-well tanks and dehydration units at VOC/HAP emissions of 6 tpy or more; truck loading controls statewide at 6 tpy or more (restated from DEQ 2016 release).

quoteSource.name: Wyoming DEQ: Oil and Gas Guidance release (May 12, 2016)

programs.name: UGRB ozone requirements and redesignation
programs.description: DEQ adopted enforceable reductions for the Upper Green River Basin and is preparing a redesignation request with a 20-year maintenance plan.

programs.name: NSPS OOOOb emergency rule (2024)
programs.description: Emergency rule incorporating 40 CFR Part 60 subpart OOOOb (effective federally May 7, 2024) so DEQ keeps primacy, with a regular rulemaking to follow.
